transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm here because I feel like once I start eating after my night shifts, I can't stop or control how much I'm eating. It's really starting to worry me, so I decided to seek some help.
Do you often feel a loss of control over how much you're eating during these episodes, like you can't stop even if you wanted to?

Yes, definitely. Once I start, it feels like a switch in my brain just flips off and I'm on autopilot. Even when I'm telling myself to stop because it's too much, I literally can't make myself put the food down until everything in front of me is completely gone.
Do these episodes of uncontrolled eating only happen during the night, typically after waking up, or do they also occur at other times of the day?

They mostly happen late at night or in the early morning after I finish my cleaning shifts, or when I'm staying up late avoiding my schoolwork. I'm not waking up from sleep to eat; I'm already awake during those hours. It doesn't really happen during the normal daytime.
Do these nighttime eating episodes ever occur after you've woken up from sleep, or are they only happening when you're already awake during the night for work or other reasons?
No, I never wake up from sleep to eat. These episodes only happen when I am already awake, like right after I finish a long night shift or when I'm staying up late avoiding my school and design work.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F50.5", "F55.8"], but based on this conversation, F55.8 (Other specified nonorganic sleep disorders) is no longer likely because the patient explicitly states they do not wake up from sleep to eat and are already awake during the nighttime eating episodes. This rules out nocturnal eating syndrome associated with sleep-wake disturbances. Instead, the pattern of recurrent episodes of night eating with a clear loss of control, occurring specifically during prolonged evening or night waking hours (post-shift or while avoiding work), aligns more closely with Night Eating Syndrome under F50.5 (Binge eating disorder), which can have a circadian pattern. The absence of daytime bingeing and the specific timing support this diagnosis. No further clarification is needed.
